introduction.text: Piazza Navona is a historic public square in Rome built on the site of the ancient Stadium of Domitian. It is renowned for its Baroque architecture, iconic fountains, and vibrant cultural life.

history.description: The site was originally the Stadium of Domitian, built by Emperor Titus Flavius Domitianus in 80 AD.
After the fall of the Western Roman Empire in 476 AD, the stadium fell into ruin and was quarried for building materials.
In the late 15th century, the city market was moved to the piazza, establishing it as a public space.
In 1574, Giacomo della Porta sculpted the Fountain of Neptune.
In 1575, Giacomo della Porta created the Fontana del Moro.
During the pontificate of Pope Innocent X (1644–1655), the piazza was transformed into a Baroque masterpiece.
In 1651, Gian Lorenzo Bernini completed the Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi, the central fountain of the piazza.
From 1652 until 1866, the piazza hosted weekly festivals that flooded the square in August.
In 1673, Bernini added a statue of a Moor wrestling with a dolphin to the Fontana del Moro.
In the 19th century, the pavement level was raised.
In 1869, the market was relocated from Piazza Navona to Campo de' Fiori.
In 1878, a statue of Neptune by Antonio Della Bitta was added to the Fountain of Neptune.
In 2011, the Fontana del Moro was vandalized when a man damaged the fountain.

design.description: The piazza showcases Baroque architecture, including the oval layout and the integration of fountains and churches.
The Church of Sant'Agnese in Agone, designed by Francesco Borromini, exemplifies Baroque church architecture.
The Palazzo Pamphili, facing the piazza, was designed by Girolamo Rainaldi and features a long gallery by Borromini.

art.description: The Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi, completed by Bernini in 1651, is the central fountain of the piazza.
The Fontana del Moro, created by Giacomo della Porta in 1575 and later enhanced by Bernini in 1673, features a Moor wrestling with a dolphin.
The Fountain of Neptune, sculpted by Giacomo della Porta in 1574, was later balanced by a statue of Neptune added in 1878.
The obelisk of Domitian, originally from the Circus of Maxentius, crowns the Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi.
